div.head: Ordal 1
div.ab: And of þam órdale we [be]beodað Godes bebodum ⁊ þæs arcebiscopes ⁊ ealra biscopa, þæt nán mann ne cúme innon þære ciricean, siððan man þæt fýr inbyrð, þe man þæt órdal mid hǽtan sceal, buton se mæssepreost ⁊ se ðe þartó gán sceal.

De ordalio precipimus in nomine Dei et precepto archiepiscopi et omnium episcoporum, ne aliquis intret in ecclesiam, postquam infertur ignis, unde iudicium calefieri debet, preter presbiterum et eum qui ad iudicium ire debet (iturus est).

And of þam órdale we bebeodað Godes bebodum and þæs arcebiscopes and ealra bisceopa, þæt nán mann ne cúme innon þære ciricean, siððan man þæt fýr inbyrð, þe man þæt órdal mid hǽtan sceal, buton se mæssepreost and se þe þartó gán sceal;

Und betreffend das Ordal gebieten wir kraft der Gebote Gottes und des Erzbischofs [von Canterbury] und aller Bischöfe, dass niemand in die Kirche hinein komme, sobald das Feuer hineingetragen wird, womit das Ordal[eisen oder -wasser] erhitzt werden soll, ausgenommen der Priester und wer dort zu[m Ordal] schreiten soll.

And concerning the ordeal we command, by the commands of God and of the archbishop [of Canterbury] and of all the bishops, that no one come into the church once the fire is carried in with which the ordeal [iron or water] is to be heated, except the priest and whoever is to go to [the ordeal] there.

And with regard to the ordeal, by the commands of God and of the archbishop and all the bishops, we enjoin that no one shall enter the church after the fire with which the iron or water for the ordeal is to be heated has been brought in, except the mass-priest and him who has to go to trial.

note.label: shares phrases
note.quote: It also shares phrases with Æthelstan's ordeal laws [n. Ord. 1, 4, 6, II As 23:2]

div.note: In H the second ‘be’ of ‘[be]beodað’ is written above the line; ‘biscopa’ was altered to ‘bisceopa’. Liebermann compares II As 23.2. Attenborough prints Liebermann’s 1 and 1a as a single section, 1; his text and translation are divided here to match Liebermann.

nicht ‘angebrannt’ (Schmid, verwechselnd mit byrneð).—Noch fehlt bischöfliche Aufsicht; s. Gl Ordal 13; Feuerordal 2; Eisenordal 6b. 9. c.—Noch 1319 sagt zu Edward II. sein des Verrates bezichtigter Vetter Graf Thomas von Lancaster: in ferro candenti offero me purgaturum; Mon. Malmesber. ed. Stubbs Chron. of Edw. II 249

Not ‘burnt’ (Schmid, confusing it with byrneð).—There is as yet no episcopal supervision; see Gl Ordal 13; Feuerordal 2; Eisenordal 6b. 9. c.—As late as 1319 Earl Thomas of Lancaster, Edward II's cousin, accused of treason, says to him: in ferro candenti offero me purgaturum; Mon. Malmesber. ed. Stubbs Chron. of Edw. II 249
